Fig. 1:Overview of PhysioWave-T, shown for EEG. (a) Channel count and sampling
rate select a route-specific front end. (b) Adaptive wavelet decomposition and
dynamic scale folding produce oneC×TC\times Tsignal. (c) Spectral importance
of clean-view tokens selects masked patches, zeroed before the online front
end. (d) A shared Transformer and two MLP heads reconstruct raw and
folded-wavelet patches against stop-gradient targets.

Fig. 3:Cross-scale channel-aggregation feed-forward network (CAFFN). The current approximation–detail pair is refined through convolution, channel aggregation, and attention to shallower-level features.

Fig. 4:Masked reconstruction on four EEG routes spanning 19–128 channels,
with 70 % of patches masked. (a) Raw-EEG head. (b) Folded-wavelet head.
Columns show the target, masked input, reconstruction, and absolute error on
masked patches;rris the masked-patch correlation. Each row shows the
median-NMSE validation window of its route, with target-derived color limits.

Fig. 6:Reliability-aware latent fusion (RALF) of 4-s EEG, ECG, and EMG windows. Reliability scores gate tokens and weight unimodal predictions. Orange symbols denote training losses; the trace shows seizure probability over a 60-s test excerpt with a 0.5 threshold.

Fig. 9:Spatial structure in channel embeddings. (a) Embedding similarity versus geodesic scalp distance, with an untrained table for comparison. (b) Electrode-centered similarity maps; links mark the five nearest neighbors.

Fig. 11:Scale allocation across sleep stages. (a) Stage-wise folding weights with 95 % subject-level confidence intervals. (b) Within-subject changes relative to wake. (c) Slowest-scale weight versusδ\delta-band power share. Rows show Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz.
